title: Jean Hammond (LearnLaunch co-founder, EdTech angel investor) — 'a treasure trove of structural methods that work to keep the mission in business'
summary: Jean Hammond — co-founder of LearnLaunch and one of Boston's most prolific EdTech angel investors — writes Eric a reader review of Incorruptible reframing the book's argument as a deep look at how a narrow interpretation of corporate purpose drives damaging outcomes for companies, people, and society. Eric surfaced it on LinkedIn.
blockquote:
Eric has a powerful way with words. In this book we have to open our eyes and ears to see a series of complex interaction of governance, power, and purpose. He dances us through multiple examples of how a narrow interpretation of the goal of corporation has driven companies, people and society to damaging outcomes.

With lots of illustrations, he shows positive and negative examples. Often showing how (and sometimes why) incoherence creeps in in the pursuit of profits. He has unearthed a treasure trove of structural methods that work to keep the mission in business.
blockquote_source: Jean Hammond, via Eric Ries on LinkedIn
